title: How to (Accidentally) Tell Old Money from New Money in Lahore. Tip #1
body: Old money says "we're in Gulberg." New money says "we're in Phase 8, Sector C." One has a house number, the other has a house name on a plaque. Old money's kitchen hasn't been touched since 1994 and there is no plan to touch it. New money renovated last year and will tell you the per-square-foot. It's a sealed deal when you notice the lawn at the older house is too big to maintain and nobody is maintaining it.

title: How to (Accidentally) Tell Old Money from New Money in Lahore. Tip #2
body: Old money drives a 2009 Land Cruiser with a scratch down one side. New money drives something German, two years old, ceramic coated, washed twice a week at the place off Main Boulevard. Both cost the same. Only one is trying. It's a sealed deal if the old car's driver has been with that family longer than the new family has had money.

title: How to (Accidentally) Tell Old Money from New Money in Lahore. Tip #3
body: Listen to how the school gets said. Old money says "Aitchison" once, flat, and moves on, because everyone already worked it out. New money says the school and then mentions the fees. Identical information. Completely different transaction. It's a sealed deal if someone adds "my father was there too" and clearly considers it unremarkable.

title: How to (Accidentally) Tell Old Money from New Money in Lahore. Tip #4
body: Old money holds the wedding at the house with eight hundred people and food from a cook nobody can hire. New money books Royal Palm and the singer's fee gets discussed for a week afterwards. The spend is the same. Only one wants a number in circulation. It's a sealed deal if a garden has hosted four generations of the same family's weddings.

title: How to (Accidentally) Tell Old Money from New Money in Lahore. Tip #5
body: The club splits it instantly. "We're Gymkhana" because the grandfather was, and the waiting list is a story other people tell. New money applied in 2016, knows someone on the committee, and is still waiting. This is the one thing money cannot speed up and it makes people genuinely unwell. It's a sealed deal if a family walks in without signing anything.

title: How to (Accidentally) Tell Old Money from New Money in Lahore. Tip #6
body: Check the phone. New money has the newest iPhone, visible, and an Apple Watch. Old money has a cracked screen on a model from two years ago and has not thought about it once. The bank balances are not different. The need to be seen is the entire difference. It's a sealed deal if the person with the cracked screen owns the building you're sitting in.

title: How to (Accidentally) Tell Old Money from New Money in Lahore. Tip #7
body: Ask about the business and count the words. "Textiles." Full stop. Any follow-up gets a polite non-answer, because the mills have been there since the sixties. New money describes a portfolio, four ventures and a franchise, and one is earning. It's a sealed deal if the answer is one word and the second question goes nowhere pleasant.

title: How to (Accidentally) Tell Old Money from New Money in Lahore. Tip #8
body: Here's what nobody admits: new money is having a better time. Better parties, better cars, actual enthusiasm about being alive. Old money is in a house that needs rewiring, being quietly certain, and faintly bored by all of it. Everyone claims to respect the second and everyone wants the invitation from the first. It's a sealed deal when a family has been rich long enough to find it dull.
